comment: Independent C-first gnomish Wizard with the default symset and msg_window:full. #name calls the starting kitten by a getlin answer whose first three bytes are 0xE1 0xBC 0x80 (the UTF-8 form of U+1F00), then #chat south prints a message that begins with that name. Ctrl-P lists the history in a text window: wintty.c process_text_window()'s `(*cp & 0x80)` arm sends the first byte through g_putch(), which outside a UTF8 or IBM symset calls graph_on() and prints the byte with its high bit stripped, so recorder patch 006 stores 'a' as a DEC graphics cell one column right of the line start; the two bytes after it are negative chars the putchar() hook ignores, so the cell survives (step 25).
